rationale: The `part_of` split for `@import` in the plain-file form, pinned in both directions by ONE file. Sass and Less INLINE a plain-file import at compile time, so the imported source becomes part of this stylesheet and the edge is an inclusion — `part_of` with `partRole:"library"` (this file is the library: it carries the directive naming its part). A `@import` that loads a stylesheet keeps `imports`. The grammar answers the question as a SHAPE, not a spelling, so the fixture puts one shape per line, and the discriminator is: exactly ONE named child, its type `string_value`, the specifier not ending `.css`, and not a `//`/`http(s)://` protocol URL nor a `sass:`/`data:` scheme. line 8 is the fire case; lines 9-13 are the five must-not classes, each failing a DIFFERENT half of the predicate (suffix / child type / second child / protocol / scheme), which is what stops a later widening of any one condition from passing silently. The label move is NOT a gain or a loss: source, target, line and the project-file claim are unchanged, so both `expectRelationships` and `forbidRelationships` pin the same (from,target,line) triple in opposite labels.
